doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Alan Dawson and Tony Williams
summary: He praises Alan Dawson's clean finger control and gentlemanliness, and recalls Tony Williams as a teenage Miles sideman and a late phone message.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I’m going to try to get there to interview Joe Harris that’s for sure. You were talking about Alan Dawson, how about his sterling student?

Alan, man, I was very impressed with Alan. Alan was a clean player, man. Everything he did, he made, he had tremendous finger control, man, and stick control. He got a good sound and rhythm man. He was dynamite, you know.
And a great teacher, man. Very nice guy too, you know.
Yeah, he was. That’s a good word, man. He was a gentleman, you know, which is cool.
How about his most famous student, Tony Williams?

(Unintelligible) Tony. Let me tell you about Tony, man. I see Tony one night and man he’s so happy to see me here. Where was he, Birdland? Went to Birdland, right, and about a week later, I’m gone and I come back and on my answering service Tony called me, but in the meantime man, he had passed away.
Which it was strange to hear his voice and knowing that he had passed.
When did he pass? I know it wasn’t ‘97?
Well I met Tony in San Francisco when he was with Miles. He came out -­
No, he wasn’t 20, he was 18, something like that. And I was kind of one of his heroes, you know. He was cool.
